title: Agent skill: choose and check structural, heat and flow models
body:
## What and why

Closes #481. An agent can call modelling commands without establishing whether the chosen idealisation answers the engineering question. The new `skills/fieldcraft-modelling/SKILL.md` supplies a concise decision procedure for units and material evidence, physics-appropriate elements, loads/supports, symmetry, interfaces, step activity, and quantitative checks before drawing an engineering conclusion.

The skill routes parameter discovery to the running version's command schemas and meshing decisions to the existing meshing skill. It distinguishes total versus per-node force, singular local solid stresses, excluded symmetry modes, ties versus opening/sliding contact and thermal resistance, physical transients versus accelerated steady iterations, and single-fluid held-wall flow versus a verified coupled exchanger. Sources are public primary references with original paraphrases; no proprietary procedure, figure, data library or input deck is copied.

A short linked reference provides two original runnable JSON exercises: axial rod extension/reaction and steady prism conduction with independent hand calculations, display-unit invariance and a second mesh. It also describes how to interrogate the existing heated-flow sample honestly. All four changed files are skill/reference text or small original recipes. Production code, solver numerics, dependencies, MCP prompt registration and ROADMAP are unchanged.

## Demonstration

The 33-second native app clip applies the skill to current functionality: an original synthetic conductor's temperature/heat-flow checks, then temperature and signed wall heat in the existing heated-air bracket example. The selected frames are captured from the actual presented native window, with the RTX 4090 Vulkan viewport visible. The flow solve uses the CPU and three threads; viewport rendering is not described as a GPU fluid solve.

Captions identify the conductor as an exactly representable synthetic patch, then the flow's one air domain, held-hot bracket, 5 mm spacing and physical 45-second transient. They preserve the density-variation warnings: 15.9% with dt 0.25 s/180 steps and 3.5% after halving dt to 0.125 s/360 steps at the same physical duration. Both runs remain coarse smoke/sensitivity evidence, with no steady-state, heat-rate accuracy, cooling-solid or two-fluid exchanger claim.

The reused developer executable was originally built at `99d8536` during an earlier owned worktree layer; its SHA-256 is `ff37388057d4eee4dd5490a4e927c45be6c20dcbf3fae4766dad2355d3a606c0`. Its production app/engine/solver source is identical to the `7d9c027d71b2c1ea3395e2552e95f0455a7244db` branch base: the earlier Rust diff is confined to updater test code. It was not rebuilt at this docs commit, and the documentation/recipes introduce no new runtime behavior. No DX12 or DXC operation is part of this demonstration; the actual viewport is Vulkan.

`modelling-checks.mp4`, `conduction-check.png` and `heated-flow-check.png` were normal-pushed as ordinary Git blobs by the coordinator in artifact-queue commit `1f57cdd54b986accdcbe4b2340775abcbce77512`, under `objects/docs/modelling-skill-481/443160e0bbc3c6a8f8310c1366bb6e593eb6eda6/`. Index SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes were verified before the push. The maintainer's receipts confirm all three artifacts received, with SHA-256 hashes and byte counts matching their manifests; `github_attachment` is now `attached` with the verified native URLs below. Original capture/encoding recipes, raw command responses, numerical checks and safe provenance are retained externally. No demo media or LFS pointers are in the feature history.

## Validation

- The skill-creator `quick_validate.py` passes; frontmatter, description/name and scaffold checks pass. All relative Markdown references resolve. The 22 exact engine command IDs referenced by the skill/recipes exist in the live command catalogue, and both complete recipes execute through the actual native engine.
- Original axial rod: extension 4.285714285714285e-5 m versus F L/(E A), stress 9,999,999.999999996 Pa versus 10 MPa, root reaction -999.9999999999999 N balancing 1000 N. Changing only display units reports 0.04285714285714285 mm and 9.999999999999996 MPa for the same model.
- Original conductor: coarse 2x3x6 and fine 4x6x12 hex8 grids give midpoint 323.15 K and axial flux -7500 W/m2. Opposite end heat reactions have magnitude 4.5 W; their imbalance is below 1.4e-12 W on both meshes. Both `model.check` results have zero errors and warnings. These exact linear fields verify the setup, not asymptotic convergence of a realistic part.
- The existing heated-flow sample passes `model.check` and both explicit CPU solves, returning 5824 total/5504 fluid cells and 45 s end time. Actual density warnings and remaining limitations are preserved above. No unmapped raw `final_max_speed`/`max_speed_time` values are presented under display-unit labels; the demonstration uses deliberate SI display units and temperature/heat fields.
- Public primary sources checked directly: NIST material-property data evaluation, University of Illinois axial loading, Wood et al. NAFEMS 2015 singularity paper, and NASA verification/validation/spatial-convergence guidance. Only concepts are paraphrased.
- `git diff --check` passes; fresh fork `upstream-develop` rebase was a no-op before normal feature push. No Rust code changed, so no new Cargo build, broad test/clippy/wasm gate or numerical oracle run was needed. No existing fixture was blessed or tolerance widened.

- Relayed CI on this exact head: main `cargo xtask ci`, heavy tests and oracle succeeded. Windows app and macOS oracle jobs were skipped, not runtime passes.

## Known limitations

A skill improves setup and reporting decisions; it does not add physics or certify an analysis. The small synthetic examples use assumed material properties and are implementation checks, not experimental validation, material allowables or converged local design stresses. Equal results on an exactly representable patch do not demonstrate convergence order on curved or difficult geometry.

The heated-flow example retains a visible weak-compressibility warning even at the smaller time step. Its spatial grid, mass/energy balance and thermal accuracy have not been established as a design-quality exchanger calculation. The held-temperature solid neither cools nor conducts internally in this example; there is no second fluid circuit. Coupled-exchanger and GPU LES/fan/porous work must be checked against actual available verified capabilities, not inferred from this skill or an open PR. The separately reported fluid reply-unit omission is not fixed here.

The native demonstration was run on Windows only. It is a documentation/recipe change with unchanged production source, and does not claim new UI/backend behavior or platform runtime validation.
